content.text: Emphasis inside a rejected reference link now works. The bug report's example gives `[foo bar baz qux]ref`, and so do the `_`, `**` and CommonMark example 533 versions. All spec and unit tests pass. **Cause:** before it starts reading the inline text, `Lexer.inlineTokens` hides parts of the text from the emphasis code: links, escapes, code spans and HTML. Any `[text][ref]` whose `ref` is defined gets hidden as one whole block, which stops emphasis from reaching into or out of a link. But if the link text holds another link, CommonMark says to reject the outer link. Marked did reject it and read the text again as plain inline content, but the text stayed hidden. So the `*` inside could never find its closing `*` and came out as a literal asterisk. **Fix, in `src/Lexer.ts`:** - I moved the hiding step into a private helper, `maskInlineSrc(src)`, without changing what it does. - In the inline loop, when a reference link matches but gets rejected, the rest of the text is hidden again from just after the `[`. The inner link and the trailing `[ref]` stay hidden, and the emphasis delimiters in between become visible. Strikethrough (`~~`) in that spot now works too. This re-hiding only happens on that rejection, so normal text costs nothing extra. **Tests:** - Example 533 was marked `shouldFail` in both `test/specs/commonmark/commonmark.0.31.2.json` and `test/specs/gfm/commonmark.0.31.2.json`. It passes now, so I removed the marker. - I added a regression test, `test/specs/new/em_in_rejected_reflink.md/.html`. It covers `*`, `_` and `**`, an inner reference link, and emphasis wrapped around a rejected link. - Results: spec tests 1789 pass, 0 fail. The marked, Lexer, Parser, Hooks and instance unit tests all pass. I couldn't run `tsc --noEmit` or `eslint` because those commands were denied permission. The esbuild build succeeded. One edge case isn't handled. An emphasis opener that comes *before* a rejected reference link still sees that link as hidden when it looks for its closer. That only matters if the matching closer is inside the rejected link's text, which is rare. The common case, `*a [foo [b](/url)][ref] c*`, is covered by the new test.
